classification.difficultyReason: Estimate the biased-die probability from a frequency table and scale it to 1500 rolls.

content.prompt:
Jeremy rolled a biased 6-sided die a number of times. He recorded the results in the table.
How many times would he expect to roll a 3 if he rolled the die 1500 times?

spec.description: Editable two-row mathematical table, left-positioned, with a wide label column, centred numbers, one horizontal divider, vertical separators and a right border. No top, bottom or left outer border.
spec.answerVisibility: All table entries are student-visible givens.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total trials} &= 23+19+48+20+21+19\\\text{Total trials} &= 150\\\text{Relative frequency of 3} &= \frac{48}{150}\\\text{Expected frequency} &= \text{Relative frequency}\times\text{Total trials}\\\text{Expected frequency} &= \frac{48}{150}\times1500\\\text{Expected frequency} &= 480\end{align*}$$
He would expect to roll a 3 approximately 480 times.
